newsitem.title: USA: Duke Oconee nuke start delayed to midweek.
newsitem.headline: Duke Oconee nuke start delayed to midweek.

text.p: Duke Power Co has delayed electricity production from its 846 megawatt (MW) Oconee nuclear power unit 2 to mid-week during continued startup testing, a company spokesman said Monday.
The unit, located in Seneca, S.C., was originally expected to resume power production over the weekend, but spokesman Rick Zuercher said that date has been pushed back to near Jan 29.
"We are still involved in some startup activities," Zuercher said.
Oconee unit 2 was shut Sept 24 after a steam pipe burst in the non-nuclear side of the plant, scalding seven workers.
The adjacent Oconee units 1 and 3, each with a capacity of 846 MW, were shut Oct 4 for steam pipe inspections and were expected to resume operations in February.
Duke Power has a total generating capacity of about 18,500 MW, of which the Oconee plant accounts for about 14 percent.
